tossups.text: The Verinag Spring, located within this geographical region, is the source of the Jhelum (JELL-UM) River. China claims the Aksai Chin in this area, which includes the Ladakh district of another country. The Line of Control is located here. Located between the Pir Panjal and Karakoram Ranges, this territory has two different regional capitals at Muzaffarabad and Srinagar. Goat husbandry in this region lent its name to a type of wool. It's located northeast of Punjab. A state is named for Jammu and this region, once called "Heaven on Earth" by Mughal emperors. For 10 points, name this region fiercely contested between Pakistan and India.

This man's rule was secured by the victory at the Battle of Celaya. At the end of his term in office, he campaigned for the election of Ignacio Bonillas and tried to steal some of the treasury, but was killed while fleeing to Veracruz. He was serving as governor of Coahuila when he first chose to rebel, and he was the military leader of the Constitutionalist Army, which campaigned to displace the assassin of his former confederate Francisco Madero. He successfully maintained World War I neutrality, but he frustrated the United States by opposing Pershing's incursion. Succeeded by Alvaro Obregón, this opponent of Victoriano Huerta had problems consolidating his rule due to his more radical associates, Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata. For 10 points, name this rebel against Porfirio Díaz who became the first president of the Mexican Republic.

In a story by this author, the protagonist reads Arabian Nights in a cafe before fighting three drunk men who had thrown bread crumbs at him. In a different story by this author, the protagonist boards a train to Ashgrove to avoid the MI5 agent Richard Madden. This author of "The South" wrote a story in which the protagonist murders a sinologist to convey the location of a British artillery park. In a story by this author, purifiers destroy "nonsense" books in the title location, which is made up of an infinite number of hexagonal rooms. Many of this author's short stories were published in his collection Ficciones. For 10 points, name this Argentinian author of "The Garden of Forking Paths" and "The Library of Babel".

One character with this profession notes that it's impossible to draw a girl towards you "as if you had just been given a copy of the first, suppressed edition of Madame Bovary," as there was never such an edition. That character with this profession says he didn't kill his adulterous wife Ellen; he ended her life by cutting off life support after a suicide attempt left her in a coma. Geoffrey Braithwaite, the narrator of Flaubert's Parrot, has this profession, as does a man who skips Mr. Turton's bridge party and yells at a woman after seeing her inside a mosque. That character with this profession accidentally incriminates himself after he picks up a pair of field glasses, and is falsely accused of rape by Adela Quested in E.M. Forster's A Passage to India. For 10 points, name this profession shared by Aziz and a man who turns into an evil alter ego, Henry Jekyll.

A poem set in this region declares, "that night on the marge of Lake Lebarge / I cremated Sam McGee," and is by this region's "bard," Robert Service. At the end of a story set in this region, the narrator murmurs "You were right" to the old man of Sulphur Creek. A character who is transported from California's Santa Clara Valley to work in this region watches most of his companions die while working for Hal and Mercedes. A character freezes to death in this region in the story "To Build a Fire." John Thornton frees Buck from working as a sled dog for miners exploring this region. For 10 points, The Call of the Wild is set during a gold rush in what territory in northwest Canada?

Two diplomats from this country were accused of smuggling rubles from the Soviet Union in a 1928 scandal. The British led Operations Freshman and Gunnerside took place in this country and sabotaged a project to acquire heavy water, which could lead to the production of nuclear weapons. A man from here compiled the 1,518 page long document 2083: A European Declaration of Independence, which denounces "cultural Marxists" and "Muslims." In this country, a man dressed as a police officer traveled to a youth summer camp and killed 69 people. During World War II, it was led by puppet Nazi stooge Vidkun Quisling. For 10 points, name this Scandinavian country, the site of horrific 2011 shootings carried out by Anders Breivik.

Its thirty-fourth section describes the massacre at Goliad, and another section labels gods like Zeus, Odin, and Mexitli "the old cautious hucksters." The narrator calls a Corpse "good manure" that does not offend him and tells Death "it is idle to / try to alarm me." That narrator also asks how he extracts strength from the beef he eats, and calls grass "the beautiful uncut hair of graves." In its final section, the speaker departs "as air" after sounding "his barbaric yawp over the roofs of the world." Ending with the line "I stop somewhere waiting for you," FTP, name this poem divided into 52 sections in the 1867 edition of Leaves of Grass, the masterpiece of Walt Whitman.

One person with this name composed the verse novel Aurora Leigh. Another poet with this name wrote The Ring and the Book and composed poems about the "Pied Piper of Hamelin" and "Porpheria's Lover." One person with this name wrote "How do I love thee? Let me count the ways" in Sonnets from the Portuguese, and another composed My Last Duchess. For 10 points, give this shared surname of the Romantic poets Elizabeth Barrett and Robert.

When immersed in potassium dichromate and silver nitrate, these cells turn black in Golgi staining. The synthesis of proteins in these cells takes place in Nissl (NISS-uhl) bodies. Coming in two varieties, these cells can come in pyramidal and multipolar varieties. Parts of these entities include the Nodes of Ranvier, the soma, and these also possess dendrites and axons. For 10 points, name these specialized cells that connect to each other to form networks in the body's central and peripheral nervous systems.

Joshua Cushman was a member of a group of six congressmen strongly opposed to this legislation, and claimed it would result in a "pestiferous mischief" that would "take deep root in that luxuriant soul."A speech by Felix Walker during debates about this legislation is the origin of the word "bunk" to describe inflated rhetoric. The debates concerning this legislation also led John Randolph to coin the term doughface to refer to pliant politicians. In a letter to John Holmes, an elderly Thomas Jefferson described this legislation as the "knell of the Union." The Tallmadge Amendment was not added to this legislation, though thanks to the Thomas proviso, it did prevent slavery north of the 36-30 parallel with the exception of one territory. Maine became a free state because of, for 10 points, what 1820 legislation that also admitted a namesake midwestern slave state?
acceptableAnswers: Tallmadge amendment until it is read

tossups.text: The "cloud-in-cloud problem" is caused by a function whose independent variable is this quantity; the derivation of that function of this quantity introduces a factor of two without any real justification. A function of this quantity was derived from an excursion set model based on ellipsoidal collapse with a moving barrier by Ravi K. Sheth and Giuseppe Tormen. An initial Gaussian density fluctuation field is used to derive an abundance function of this quantity in a seminal 1974 paper by (+) William H. Press and Paul Schechter. A common way to calculate this quantity is to take the integral up to a radius of "r-sub-200-c" of the NFW profile. The three main methods for measuring this quantity for galaxy clusters are: inferring it from X-ray luminosity and temperature, virial analysis of the velocity distribution, and projecting it from gravitational lensing observations. The distribution of this extensive quantity inferred from rotation curves indicated that large portions of this quantity not near the center of galaxies must be accounted for by dark matter. For 10 points, name this quantity, the source of gravitational attraction.
acceptableAnswers: accept of dark matter halo mass
” prompt on amount of dark matter

tossups.text: This man meets a girl at Coachella and proceeds to get high on anesthetics in one of his albums. Tony Bergdorf has a heart attack in Las Vegas and ten thousand dollars is set aside for his widow in this 1960 film. He claims he "thought you were cool enough to kick it" in one work, but Rusty Ryan fails to convince this man to drop his vendetta against Terry Benedict, who is dating Tess, in this film. This man, a member of the Rat Pack along with Frank Sinatra and George Clooney, released Channel Orange before robbing three to five casinos, including the Bellagio. For 10 points, name this man appearing in the first of three titular films, a con-and-R&B artist.

This play's protagonist is accompanied by Xanthias on a quest to judge a competition between Aeschylus and Euripides to determine which will be returned to life to help Athens. As Dionysus crosses a lake to reach the underworld while dressed as Heracles, this play's title chorus angers him by tauntingly croaking "bre-ke-ke-kax koax koax." For 10 points, name this comedic play by Aristophanes named for a group of cheeky amphibians.

In this work, a god demands people's 'waists and armpits' in exchange for the secret of fire, and the first people created in this book are dissolved, while the second are disfigured and drowned in resin as a punishment for not having souls. According to this work, the world originally consisted only of the sea and four gods, of which the only one on the terrestrial plane was Gucumatz. The first successful people created in this book are made of corn; four men named Balam-Quitzé, Balam-Acab, Mahucutah and Iqui-Balam. Two central figures in this work are killed for playing a ball game too noisily and disturbing the lords of Xibalba, and their sons narrowly escape the same fate. For 10 points, name this text, a collection of myths such as that of the Hero Twins, and the cornerstone of Maya mythology.

At one point, this literary character meets a man looking for flowers, who boasts of a happy time in his life spent in the madhouse. This character forms a relationship with a woman called "Miss B," but her aunt and societal pressures force the couple to break up. Near the end of the novel in which he appears, this character reads of the fates of people like Salgar and Morar. This occurs during his recitation off a poem by Ossian to his love. He is friends with Albert, but is enchanted with his friend's wife, Charlotte. This character's eventual suicide with a pistol reportedly kicked off waves of copycats throughout Europe. For 10 points, name this title character whose "sorrows" were described in an epistolary novel by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.

This thinker and an alphabetically later colleague wrote a text that opens by describing the "delegates of a hundred nations" at the United Nations, in a section titled "The World Is Shrinking." This was the alphabetically prior author of a cartoon-illustrated pamphlet designed to counteract racial tension, along with Gene Weltfish. This thinker used their mentor's field notes on the Kwakiutl ("kwah-kee-OO-tull") to compare them with the Dobu and Zuni in a book that defines its title concept as "personality writ large." While consulting for the Office of War Information, this co-author of The Races of Mankind conducted an example of "anthropology at a distance" that contrasts guilt and shame cultures. For 10 points, what anthropologist wrote Patterns of Culture and a study of Japanese society titled The Chrysanthemum and the Sword?

In human physiology, this structure is essential for calcitonin. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in calcitonin.

tossups.text: Molecules in this class react with carboxylic acids to form esters in the Fischer synthesis, and they can be formed by the reaction of Grignard ("GRIN"-"yard") reagents with carbonyls. The dehydration of these molecules forms an alkene. When a functional group of this type is attached to a benzene ring, the product is called a phenol. One of the most notable examples from this class is produced by fermentation. Characterized by a hydroxyl group, identify these organic molecules that include ethanol as well as isopropyl, the "rubbing" type.

A type of these phenomena is significant only within distances on the order of the "radius of deformation." The Pierson-Moskowitz spectrum describes the distribution of these phenomena when a system is in a state of equilibrium described as "fully developed." A model of these phenomena sets zero equal to [read slowly] the time derivative of u plus the third spatial derivative of u plus 6 times u times the spatial derivative of u. The speed of these phenomena is given by the square root of the quantity g times d under an approximation that holds depth to be much less than the horizontal scale of motion. The rotation of the Earth produces large-scale examples of these phenomena named for Kelvin and Rossby. Examples of these phenomena called solitons are sometimes identified with unusually large "rogue" ones of them. For 10 points, name these phenomena whose heights measured from crest to trough.

Four of these instruments respond to the title Unanswered Question posed by the trumpets in a work by Charles Ives. The aria "Der Holle Rache" (der HER-luh RAKH-uh) is sung by the Queen of the Night in a Mozart opera titled for a magic one of these instruments. This instrument represents the bird in Peter and the Wolf and is the first to play in Grieg's "Morning Mood." For 10 points, name this high-pitched woodwind instrument, a cousin of the piccolo.

parts.text: Name this river that is also joined by the Gunnison, Green, and Gila rivers before emptying into the Gulf of California.
Formerly known as Boulder Dam, this dam on the Colorado River began construction in 1931 under the administration of its namesake President.
The Hoover Dam forms this man-made lake, the largest reservoir in the United States in terms of maximum water capacity.

bonuses.leadin: It is joined by the San Juan River at Lake Powell. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1604 meeting prompted by the thousand-signature Millenary Petition, which contained demands by the Puritans for a reformed Anglican Church to begin the reign of the new king.
The conference resulted in the creation of this book under the oversight of Richard Bancroft. This translation of the Bible eventually became the most widely printed book in history.
acceptableAnswers: King James Version of the Bible

parts.text: Before he took the English throne, James presided over one of these events in North Berwick that resulted in the deaths of Agnes Simpson and Gillis Duncan. James later discussed these events in his Daemonologie.

bonuses.leadin: Some results of this meeting included revisions to the use of the terms "absolution" and "confirmation," as well as permission to carry out baptisms in private homes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel in which Hetty discovers she is pregnant with Arthur's child and commits infanticide by abandoning the child in a field.
In this novel, the central character raises an orphaned two year old named Eppie, who is actually the daughter of Godfrey Cass. The title character's character is stolen by Dunstan Cass.
This author of Felix Holt created Maggie Tulliver in the novel The Mill on the Floss and wrote both Adam Bede and Silas Marner.

bonuses.leadin: This novel features the preacher Dinah Morris and sees Hetty Sorrel seduced by Captain Arthur Donnithorne, who leaves her to her other suitor, the title character. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author who won a Pulitzer Prize for his biography Abraham Lincoln: The War Years. He referred to the city you're sitting in as "Hog Butcher for the World."

This work by Sandburg begins "The first cry of a newborn baby in Chicago or Zamboango, in Amsterdam or Rangoon, has the same pitch and key." It concludes with a poem ending "There is only one child in the world / and the child's name is All Children."
acceptableAnswers: almost any other word instead of “prologue

parts.text: Sandburg wasn't the only American author to curate photographs with his writing. Eleven years earlier, James Agee wrote text to accompany a collaborator's photographs of sharecroppers hurt by the Great Depression, in this book.
parts.answer: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men
acceptableAnswers: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men
The Let Us Now Praise Famous Men

bonuses.leadin: The first title character considers whether to tell the second that "Life is hard; be steel; be a rock" or "Life is a soft loam; be gentle; go easy" in this author's poem "A Father to His Son." For 10 points each:

parts.text: In this Eco novel, Adso of Melk is the narrator and apprentice of friar William of Baskerville. Together, they solve a murder mystery at an abbey.
William of Baskerville's name alludes to both William of Ockham and this detective from The Hound of the Baskervilles.
In addition to The Name of the Rose, Umberto Eco wrote this book in which Belbo, Diotallevi, and Casaubon decide to create "The Plan". It is named after an object in the Musée des Arts et Métiers.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the works of Umberto Eco, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify these three diminishings of a certain nation in the late eighteenth century. Resistance to the second by Tadeusz Kosciuszko led to the third and final one in 1795.
The partitions of Poland took place during the rule of this Russian tsarina. This ruler was opposed by Pugachev's rebellion, and her favorites included Grigori Orlov and Grigori Potemkin.
In the parts of Poland that were controlled by Catherine, a "Pale of Settlement" was established as a territory for members of this religious faith.

bonuses.leadin: The second of these events was sparked by the formation of the Confederation of Targowica in response to the adoption of a new constitution in 1791. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel about the artist Hurtle Duffield, whom Don Lethbridge assists in creating the title work.
The title character of this work by the author of The Vivisector meets Laura Trevelyan at Mr. Bonner's house.
This Australian author of Memoirs of Many in One and Flaws in the Glass wrote The Vivsector and Voss.

bonuses.leadin: This novel's protagonist takes Hero Pavloussi as his mistress and serves as a companion to Rhoda Courtney. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author of Candide.
This term is often used to describe Voltaire's works. It is the use of humor to criticize other people's stupidity, especially that widespread in society.
Voltaire also wrote a work about this mythical Greek king who kills his father Laius and marries his mother Jocasta.

bonuses.leadin: His real name was Francois-Marie Arouet (frahn-SWAH mah-REE ah-roo-ETT), and his best-known work is about a young man who is taught by Pangloss that he lives in the best of all possible worlds. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this term for large astronomical bodies found orbiting stars outside our solar system. Roughly four thousand of these bodies have been discovered as of summer 2019.
Exoplanets are most often found when they make a transit of their star. When this happens, astronomers can study the chemical makeup of this envelope of gases surrounding a planet.

Exoplanets are considered more interesting if they are found in the habitable zone of their star, a zone often nicknamed for this fairy tale character. Exoplanets in this zone will be the right distance from the star and not be too hot or too cold.

bonuses.leadin: The primary mission of the Kepler Space Telescope is to find and study these objects. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this object that served as the centerpiece of the emblem for a celebration of a country's 2,500 year history, during which the dubious claim that this object is the first declaration of universal human rights was introduced.

For his 1971 celebration of the 2,500th anniversary of Iran's existence, Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi housed foreign dignitaries in a lavish tent city he set up in the ruins of this ceremonial capital of the Achaemenids.

Pahlavi's 100-rial note depicted the "audience scene" relief found on the building of this type in Persepolis. This Old Persian word denotes a hypostyle hall, and is most commonly used to name the Audience Hall at Persepolis.

bonuses.leadin: In 1971, Princess Ashraf presented U Thant with a copy of this object that now sits in the entrance lobby of the United Nations. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this occurrence, the highest energy observed from this scattering process.
The Compton edge occurs due to the Compton effect, where the shift in frequency can be calculated using this formula at high frequencies.
At low frequencies, the Klein-Nishina formula works best for this other type of scattering, which occurs for a charged particle. It is named for an English scientist.

bonuses.leadin: This phenomenon occurs in gamma ray spectroscopy when gamma ray scattering leads to the presence of ghost peaks in the resulting spectrum. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this set of six musical works that were presented to a margrave named Christian, who presided over the namesake German location of these compositions.
The Brandenburg Concertos are by this German Baroque composer, who also dedicated his A Musical Offering to Frederick the Great.

J.S. Bach's A Musical Offering features a prominent flute in its last section, which is named for this musical form. In general, this form consists of an exposition, a development, and a recapitulation.

bonuses.leadin: The fourth piece of this set of composition calls for a duo of "echo flutes." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this French drama about the titular religious hypocrite.
This French playwright of Tartuffe and The School for Wives described Harpagon, whose greed interferes with his children's marriages, in The Miser.
The title character of this Moliere play, Alceste, loves Celimene but is disappointed by her choice to remain in society rather than become a hermit with him.

bonuses.leadin: This play opens with Orgon's son Damis criticizing the title character, and later sees an officer take the title character away to prison. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In one of his usual antics, Gonggong headbutted and destroyed Mount Buzhou. Since that mountain had been holding up the sky, this wife of Fuxi (foo-she) replaced it with the legs that she severed from the turtle Ao (ah-oh).

Yu the Great is said to have killed Gonggong's nine-headed snake minion Xiangliu (she-aang-"leo") in his quest to end these natural disasters. Yu the Great eventually succeeded in stopping these disasters through the construction of a series of channels and dams.
Yu the Great was assisted by Yinglong in his struggles against Gonggong and Xiangliu. Yinglong is one of these creatures commonly associated with rain, rivers, and the underworld in Chinese myth.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about the Chinese water monster Gonggong. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these animals whose souls are harvested to build a magic flute by a man known as Johnnie Walker in another novel. A boy in that novel gains the ability to speak to these animals after the Rice Bowl Hill Incident.
Nakata speaks to cats in a novel whose protagonist is named after this author. This author wrote about Gregor Samsa's transformation into an insect in "The Metamorphosis."

This author of Kafka on the Shore wrote about a "Town of Cats" in a novel in which Aomame travels to an alternate dimension with two moons. In another of this author's novels, Toru Okada searches for his cat Mackerel.

bonuses.leadin: In a satirical novel, one of these animals encounters the student Avalon Coldmoon and mocks the teacher Mr. Sneaze. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this economist who names a curve that shows the total effect of a price change including the income and substitution effect, in contrast to one that only looks at the substitution effect.
Marshallian demand can be related to Hicksian demand through this equation, which decomposes the substitution and income effects.
Marshall created one of these works that was largely dominant in Britain titled Principles of Economics. Samuelson and Nordhaus wrote another one of these works, Economics, following Marshall's.

bonuses.leadin: This economist abandoned his physics studies after a mental crisis that turned him to Sigdwickian utilitarian. For 10 points each:

What is the main function of the bronchus in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to trachea structure.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Identify this group of elements, which have complete valence shells. These elements, which include krypton and xenon, are known for being more unreactive.
This element is the lightest noble gas, with an atomic number of two. It has an atomic symbol of He, and is commonly used to inflate balloons.

Helium was first discovered during one of these events by Jules Janssen, after he noticed a bright yellow spectral line coming from a certain entity. Namesake "beads" were observed by Francis Baily during these events.

bonuses.leadin: The first binary compound containing an element from this group that was discovered featured that element bonded to four fluorine atoms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these inorganic compounds which include Epsom salt. They are denoted with a single dot in their molecular formula.
Noble gas compound hydrates are an example of this class of compounds, in which one molecule forms a "cage" inside which the other molecule is trapped.
Clathrates are a sub-type of this class of compounds, in which one molecule forms a lattice with vacancies or cavities occupied by another molecule.

bonuses.leadin: These compounds exhibit a special type of ionization isomerism in which a certain neutral ligand enters or leaves the coordination sphere. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Austrian capital city, where Beethoven and Haydn had worked a century earlier.
Schoenberg's innovation moved away from the use of keys, instead keeping a balance between every note in the chromatic scale; thus, Schoenberg's technique is often named for this number of tones.

In 1913, Viennese listeners rioted at Schoenberg's "Skandalkonzert" [scandal concert]; a witness testified in court that the smack of a thrown punch was the most "harmonious" sound of the evening. That riot came just two months before a more famous classical music riot, at the Paris premiere of this Stravinsky ballet.
